Subject: Privacy architecture review — VPC / air-gapped options (post-call)

Hi Lucas,

Thanks for the call earlier — appreciate the clear go/no-go constraints from your side. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum:

- SOC 2: you mentioned Medixa is currently SOC 2 Type 2 in flight; want confirmation on expected completion date and whether you can accept a redacted report or an NDA first.
- GDPR / HIPAA: you called out data residency in EU for certain customers and HIPAA for a subset of workloads — we can support both via Private/VPC and on-prem models.
- Network isolation: we discussed fully isolated VPC deployment with dedicated subnets, no internet egress for inference hosts, and optional bastion for org-managed maintenance.
- Air-gapped option: there are extra steps (image signing, offline license tokens, manual update cadence) — we can provide a checklist.

Action items I have for Medixa:
1) Please share a simple infra diagram (VPC/network boundaries) and call out any on-prem constraints — attach if possible.
2) Fill out the attached vendor security questionnaire (short form) — the answers will help us scope HSM/KMS, audit log retention, and encryption requirements.
3) Confirm a 60-min technical deep-dive slot next week (we suggested Thu May 6, 10:00 PT).

Internal owners: Mina (security), Rishi (solutions), me (sales/coordination).

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_medixa.xlsx (stub)

Best,
Ben

Hi Lucas — thanks for sending the diagram.

Quick notes from security:
- SOC 2: we can accept a redacted Type 2 report under NDA. If timing is tight we can do compensating controls during procurement (e.g., limited pilot on Dedicated with extra monitoring).
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and can integrate with customer HSMs for Private deployments. For Thales HSM we typically do a KMIP bridge in the customer's VPC or a direct HSM mount in on-prem deployments.
- Air-gapped: package includes signed images, offline license key, and an installable artifact set. Update cadence is manual — we provide checksum verification instructions. We'll need your ops team to own secure media transfer.
- Audit logs & retention: by default we surface token-level and request logs to the customer's logging endpoint; retention policies can be configured per contract.

Please see attached: redwood_private_deploy_checklist.pdf (stub) — it lists minimal network flows, firewall rules, and cert/key requirements we need to validate.

Next steps I propose:
1) Medixa: share the minimal network flow diagram that shows control-plane endpoints and any outbound-only egress you require.
2) Ben/Rishi: we will prepare a short answers matrix to the questionnaire and a one-page runbook for the air-gapped install.
3) Schedule the technical deep-dive: Thu May 6, 10:00 PT — I'll join to cover compliance topics.

Mina Haddad
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
